tasks.result: DONE (bug 1 + bug 2 fixed in v3.05; helper restarted; 15-min lock removed) What changed: - Helper restarted: bayready-serve.py was NOT running on Windows (nothing on port 8765). Restarted via BayReadyServe task; pythonw PID 19260 listening on 8765. This was why the bot spammed "The Windows PC holds the bot again" every minute and did not answer /signin_inspect properly. - Bug 2 (TIS auto sign-in never opens a page) FIXED in v2.93: tgSignInAlert used else-if, so when Inspect/Xtime AND TIS were both down it only ran the Inspect sign-in and skipped TIS (yet marked TIS as "tried"). Now both auto sign-ins run in order (Inspect first, then TIS). CONFIRMED by Chanh: TIS worked on v2.96. TIS clicks its LOG IN button (debugger click at coordinates, JS click fallback) — it does not submit the form. - Bug 1 (Xtime sign-in never completes) FIXED in v3.05: v2.94-v3.04 tried Enter, form.submit(), requestSubmit(), JS clicks on "Sign in" and "Next", and a real mouse click on "Next" — the page still reported no movement. The Next click DOES get past the username step (Chanh confirmed; his photo shows the bot reached the password step with the Sign in button visible). The real cause: after the Next click the bot probed after only 2s and wrongly gave up before the page finished moving. v3.05: after the Next real click, wait 5s (plus a 3s re-probe if still on the sign-in page), then click Sign in on the password step with pressReal (real click first) and probe again. Version: BayReady v3.05. bay
tasks.lesson: A probe 2s after a click can report "no movement" while the page is still transitioning — the Next click worked (photo proves it) but the bot gave up too early. Wait 5s after a navigation click and re-probe before declaring failure. A JS click (b.click) and a real mouse click (debugger click at coordinates) are not the same: the Next button ignores the JS click but advances on the real click. When
